'''Yasaka Shrine''' (八坂神社・八阪神社, やさかじんじゃ) refers to Shinto shrines named "Yasaka." It is sometimes written as Yasaka Shrine, which is covered in another article.

These shrines are dedicated to Susanoo-no-Mikoto, the deity of Gion faith. Before the Shinbutsu bunri, Susanoo-no-Mikoto was identified with Gozu Tennō.

Other names based on Gion faith include Gion Shrines, Hiromine Shrines, Tennō Shrines, Tsushima Shrines, Yakumo Shrines, Yaegaki Shrines, Suga Shrine, Susanoo Shrine, Susa Shrine, and Hikawa Shrine (disambiguation).

Notably, some exceptions include Yasaka shrines that enshrine Yasakatome-no-Kami.

== Main Shrine ==
[[File:Yasaka Jinja.jpg|thumb|250px|right|Kyoto's Yasaka Shrine, one of the head shrines]]
* '''Yasaka Shrine''' (Higashiyama Ward, Kyoto) – Formerly Yasaka Shrine under Tendai Buddhism and Mount Hiei until the Shinto-Buddhism Separation Order. Claimed as the main shrine of Susanoo-no-Mikoto nationwide.

* ''' Yasaka Shrine''' – Enshrines Somin Shōrai.
'''Yasaka Shrine''' or '''Yasaka Jinja''' (八坂神社・八阪神社, Yasaka Jinja) refers to Shinto shrines that include "Yasaka" in their name. Some may also be written as Yasaka Shrine.

These shrines are part of Gion faith, venerating Susanoo-no-Mikoto (formerly identified with Gozu Tennō before the Shinbutsu Bunri decree).

Other shrines based on Gion Faith include Gion shrines, Hiromine Shrine, Tenno Shrine, Tsushima Shrine<ref>Tsushima Faith</ref>, Yakumo shrine, Yaegaki Shrine, Suga Shrine, Susanoo Shrine, Susa Shrine, and Hikawa Shrine<ref>Hikawa Shrine (Saitama)</ref>, among others. Their usage varies by historical period and records.

However, there are exceptions where Yasaka Shrines enshrine Yasakatome-no-Kami instead.

The Yasaka Shrine (Kyoto) in Higashiyama, Kyoto, claims to be the head shrine of all shrines dedicated to Susanoo-no-Mikoto. Before the Shinbutsu Bunri decree, it was known as Yasaka Shrine of the Tendai sect, affiliated with Mount Hiei.

[[File:Yasaka Jinja.jpg|thumb|250px|right|Yasaka Shrine (Kyoto) (One of the Head Shrines)]]
